rationale: A is more decision-useful because it gives a clearer executable path, better distinguishes live alternatives, and handles uncertainty more concretely. Its strongest advantage is practical guidance: phased recommendation, decision gates, failure modes, and a conditional pivot to managed auth. It also provides more credible quantitative framing by including outside-view base rates and explaining why estimates differ. B is solid and concise, but its engineering-quarter estimates seem less plausible given the scenario, and its composite scoring is simplistic. A better equips a careful decision-maker to act, monitor, and revise.
